title: One Piece 3D2Y: Overcome Ace’s Death! Luffy’s Vow to his Friends
summary: A 107-minute Saturday Premium special for the anime's 15th anniversary (Fuji TV, 2014-08-30), and an anime original on every primary: ONE PIECE.com's own TV-special page carries the Fuji TV planner's words 「絶対に見逃せない完全新作エピソード」 and 「描かれることがなかった修業期間中のルフィの活躍」, ja-WP calls it an アニメオリジナル作品 telling the two years 「原作では描かれなかった」, and en-WP's specials list gives the whole plot as the Byrnndi World story. The manga-derived material sits only at the two ends, and ja-WP names it as such: 「冒頭のマリンフォード頂上戦争・ルフィと仲間達とのエピソード・終盤の麦わらの一味が再集結する場面も新たに書き直されている」 (newly redrawn) — a childhood vow (ch 589), the Marineford climax through Ace's death (chs 570-574), the Rusukaina training frame (ch 597) and the Sabaody reunion and departure (chs 598-602), plus a mid-film montage of the crew's East-Blue-to-Enies-Lobby histories. Every one of those pages was already animated by the TV run, page-for-page: eps 503-504 (ch 589), eps 479-483 (chs 570-574), eps 515-516 (ch 597 pp. 2-7 / 8-19), eps 517-522 (ch 598 pp. 1-24, ch 599 pp. 2-19, ch 600 pp. 2-19, chs 601, 602) — the fandom's per-episode chapter fields and OPwiki's Umgesetzte Kapitel page ranges agree on every row where both carry data, and the unions leave no page for the special to animate first. So under T28's recap clause the bookends are a RECAP share and weigh nothing; read instead under the Shippuden-388 boundary (they are newly drawn, not recycled footage) they weigh toward FILLER, never toward canon. Filler either way, because there is no first-time coverage anywhere in the work. Oda's involvement is a design credit: ONE PIECE.com's 2014-08-18 news calls Byrnndi World an オリジナルキャラクター that 尾田栄一郎先生が描き下ろした, the screenplay is Kamisaka / Nakayama / Tanaka, and the wiki files World under 'Non-Canon Characters Designed by Oda' — nothing from the special ever entered the manga. The one thing it shows that the manga does not is the post-credits scene of Sabo setting three sake cups at Ace's and Whitebeard's grave: the manga only ever showed the RESULT, on ch 668's cover page (From the Decks of the World Vol. 48 (Final) — 'Whitebeard and Ace's Graves'), and the wiki says in as many words that 'the actual action was not seen there'. That is original animation with a cover-page tie, not an adaptation.

position.why: Confirmed as the AIR-DATE position: the special aired 2014-08-30, between ep 658 (2014-08-24) and ep 659 (2014-08-31), and the One Piece Wiki's own episode box navigates it P = Episode 658 / N = Episode 659 (Fuji TV's programme page and en-WP's specials list carry the same date; en-WP gives 107 minutes). The IN-UNIVERSE placement is a second, equally sourced fact — 516.5, the two-year gap — and is delivered in the flags for Sean to rule (the KonoSuba shape), with three ordering caveats named there.

flags_for_sean: TASK PREMISE HELD (reproduced from primaries, R3), with three corrections and two additions. (a) The Marineford share is chs 570-574, not the arc block 550-580: the beats the fandom's Long Summary names are Luffy reaching the execution platform (ch 570), Mr. 3 freeing Ace (571), the escape (572), Akainu's blow (573) and Ace dying in Luffy's arms (574) — TV eps 479-483. (b) The childhood beat is ONE scene with a home, not the Post-War block 581-597: ch 589's cliff vow after Sabo's letter ('Ace and Luffy then vow to live without regret... the two then agree to set sail on their 17th years and become pirates'), TV eps 503-504. (c) The close is exactly as the triage had it — chs 598-602, TV eps 517-522. ADDITIONS the triage did not name: the Rusukaina/'3D2Y' frame is ch 597's own pages (pp. 8-19 = ep 516, pp. 2-7 = ep 515; the fandom's Rusukaina infobox pins first = Chapter 597 / Episode 516), and there is a mid-film RECAP MONTAGE of the whole series when Luffy revives by remembering his crew — the fandom's character list carries flashback entries for Johnny/Yosaku, Kuro, Buchi, Kaya, Merry, Arlong, Patty, Carne, Zeff, Wapol, Chessmarimo, Vivi, CP9 and Spandam (East Blue to Enies Lobby). The triage's own caveat stands: NO source prints chapter numbers for the special; these are the chapters of the beats the sources name.

THE FIRST-TIME QUESTION, answered by PAGE UNIONS rather than by silence — zero pages. Every chapter the special re-tells is page-complete in the TV run: ch 597 = ep 515 (pp. 2-7) + ep 516 (pp. 8-19); ch 598 = ep 517 (pp. 1-16, 19, 23-24) + ep 518 (pp. 17-18, 20-22); ch 599 = ep 518 (pp. 2-7, 16-19) + ep 519 (pp. 8-15); ch 600 = ep 519 (pp. 2-7) + ep 520 (pp. 8-19); ch 601 = ep 521; ch 602 = ep 522; ch 573 = ep 482 (pp. 2-17); ch 574 = ep 483 (pp. 2-17) + ep 484 (pp. 16-17); ch 589 = ep 503 (pp. 2-6) + ep 504 (pp. 7-19). Two independent instruments: onepiece.fandom's per-episode `chapter =` field and opwiki.org's `Umgesetzte Kapitel`. THE CONTROL: onepiece.fandom's field is EMPTY for eps 517-522 (the known 2011-12 hole), so OPwiki carries that stretch alone — but on eps 482, 483, 484, 503, 504, 514, 515 and 516, where both sources speak, they agree page for page, which is what licenses leaning on OPwiki where the fandom is silent. No unanimated page is left for the special to animate first, and no source claims one. The wiki's only fidelity claim is 'These remade scenes more closely resemble the manga' — closer, not new.

DO NOT MISREAD THE WIKI'S 'FIRST TIME' NOTES. The 3D2Y page's Anime Notes say 'Chronologically, this TV special shows black-skinned Armament Haki for the first time', 'the first time Luffy does not shrink after using Gear 3', and 'The special also shows the NON-CANON origin of Gomu Gomu no Red Hawk'. All three are in-universe / technique firsts inside an original story — none is first-time coverage of a manga page, and the wiki labels the Red Hawk origin non-canon itself.

ODA IS A CREDIT, NOT AN ADOPTION (T26; `adopted` left null deliberately). ONE PIECE.com, 2014-08-18: 「尾田栄一郎先生が描き下ろしたオリジナルキャラクター「バーンディ・ワールド」」 — an ORIGINAL character drawn for the special; the Toei producer's comment on the licensor's own TV-special page says the same (「戦う敵は、原作者・尾田先生書き下ろしのキャラクター」); ja-WP repeats it. The screenplay is 上坂浩彦・中山智博・田中仁 (ja-WP staff list, Fuji TV's programme page, en-WP), with 原作 尾田栄一郎 the standing franchise credit that sits on every One Piece work. NOTHING CROSSED INTO THE MANGA, checked three ways: the One Piece Wiki files World under 'Non-Canon Humans' and 'Non-Canon Characters Designed by Oda' (an entire category — the pattern is recurrent and non-adoptive); the wiki's Rusukaina history wraps the whole 3D2Y paragraph in {{Non-Canon}} ... {{Non-Canon|end}} between the canon training (ch 597) and the canon departure (Return to Sabaody); and an insource search for 'Byrnndi' returns no SBS page and no chapter page. The Moa Moa no Mi, the Kyubu Kyubu no Mi, the World Pirates and the Groseade appear nowhere in Oda's pages. ja-WP does record that Fuji TV and SHUEISHA staff joined the planning from the initial stage (「フジテレビならびに集英社の担当が、製作の初期段階から打ち合わせに参加」) — a publisher's involvement in production, which is not an adoption act either.

THE ONE EDGE CASE, and why it is still not coverage — the post-credits Sabo scene. The One Piece Wiki's Sabo page carries a dedicated '3D2Y' subsection under Anime and Manga Differences: 'In the ending credit of 3D2Y, Sabo was shown placing the sake cups in front of Ace's grave. Although he did so in the manga as well, THE ACTUAL ACTION WAS NOT SEEN THERE.' The manga's witness is a COVER PAGE — ch 668's 'From the Decks of the World Vol. 48 (Final) - Whitebeard and Ace's Graves', which shows the three cups already placed (the Sabo page's trivia: 'It was later revealed that Sabo was the one who placed it there'). So the special animates an off-page event whose only manga witness is a cover-story illustration: original animation with a COVER-PAGE tie, weight SLIVER at most, never an anchor (A1 / A44), and not a page of the instrument's narrative. SOURCE-HYGIENE CAUTION for whoever reads that subsection next: its trailing sentence about 'the conversation between Luffy and Sabo during their reunion' looks misplaced — 3D2Y has no Luffy/Sabo reunion (Sabo is alone at the grave and his face is not shown); the sentence duplicates the point made in the Dressrosa-arc subsection below it about ep 663's added dialogue versus ch 794. Related and true: the special preceded Sabo's adult anime debut in ep 663, which the wiki calls 'potentially major spoilers'.

POSITION — TWO SOURCED FACTS; Sean rules which one orders the ledger (the KonoSuba shape). (1) AIR DATE, 658.5, which is what is stored and what I confirm: 2014-08-30, between ep 658 (2014-08-24) and ep 659 (2014-08-31); the fandom's episode box navigates P = Episode 658 / N = Episode 659. (2) IN-UNIVERSE, 516.5: en-WP's List of One Piece television specials states that the training 'takes place prior to season fifteen of the TV series and during volume sixty one of the manga' — en-WP's season 15 opens at ep 517 and the fandom's Volume 61 is chs 595-603, i.e. the gap the volume straddles between ch 597 and ch 598; the fandom's 3D2Y page: 'The special takes place during the two-year interlude before the Straw Hats reunite on the Sabaody Archipelago'; ja-WP: the two years 「マリンフォード頂上戦争からシャボンディ諸島再集結まで」; and the wiki's own Rusukaina history places the 3D2Y block between the Post-War training and the Return to Sabaody departure. THREE ORDERING CAVEATS if 516.5 is ever chosen: (a) the special's coda animates the reunion and the departure for Fish-Man Island — eps 517-522's own content — so a 516.5 viewer meets that material here first; (b) the post-credits Sabo scene precedes his adult anime debut (ep 663); (c) Sakazuki wears the Fleet Admiral coat with Kuzan conspicuously absent, which the manga does not reveal until ch 650 pp. 4-7 (ep 570) — the fandom's own Anime Note raises this.

THE `recap` FIELD IS FALSE ON PURPOSE — say what the field means and it need not be guessed again. This work is NOT a compilation: the licensor calls it 完全新作エピソード, ja-WP a 2時間スペシャル番組, and the stored kind `special` is right. The recap is a SHARE at both ends (T28's recap clause: re-told material of chapters already covered, weightless), not the work's form. If the ledger's flag means 'contains a recap share' rather than 'is a recap work', flip it. PROPOSED LEDGER NOTE if one is wanted: 'Anime-original (完全新作エピソード): the Byrnndi World story inside the two-year gap. The bookends re-tell chapters the TV run already animated — ch 589 (eps 503-504), chs 570-574 (eps 479-483), ch 597 (eps 515-516), chs 598-602 (eps 517-522) — recap, weightless under T28; zero first-time coverage. Oda drew the villain: a credit, never an adoption (T26). In-universe placement 516.5.'

SIZING TIER, stated honestly. No timestamped source exists for the share split (animefillerlist / animefillerguide do not list One Piece's TV specials), so the sizing here is by BEATS from two independent plot summaries: the fandom's Long Summary gives the prologue one paragraph of fourteen and the coda part of one, and en-WP's summary is a single paragraph of the World plot closing on one sentence ('Six months later, Luffy reunites with his crew'). The standing does not turn on the size — with zero first-time coverage there is no canon share to weigh, so neither T28's materiality bar nor the sole-adaptation exception can be reached.

NOVELIZATION TRAP for any later join: JUMP j BOOKS published a 3D2Y novelization on 2014-10-03 (ja-WP; the article's external link to j-books.shueisha.co.jp), and ja-WP cites 小説版第二章 for World's ฿500,000,000 bounty. That book is an adaptation OF the special, never its source, and it is not Oda's. The Blu-ray / DVD shipped 2014-11-27. AniList's `source: MANGA` tag and its SIDE_STORY edge are franchise metadata, not a chapter claim.

NO REPAIRS. Stored title, date (2014-08-30 — Fuji TV's own programme page, ja-WP, en-WP and the fandom all agree), kind (`special`: a 土曜プレミアム two-hour slot, not a film and not a compilation) and the 107-minute runtime (en-WP) all check out against the halo row.

BY-CATCH, outside this ask: en-WP files the very next special, SP9 'Episode of Sabo' (2015-08-22), as 'an abridged remake' — a different shape from this one (a re-adaptation of already-adapted chapters, the zatch-bell class, where overlap never proves filler), and the fandom notes that 'the scene of Sabo visiting Ace's grave from Episode of Sabo was used in the following episode'. If Episode of Sabo sits on this shelf it needs its own per-work verdict; do not carry this filler ruling across to it.
